title: Progress indicator
overview: Where they are in a multi-step or multi-task journey.
apply_when: Wizard, onboarding, returnable tasks with named states.
not_when: Unknown-duration wait (loading_indicator), placeholder geometry (skeleton), or spinner on Submit (button loading).

vs.why: wait with unknown duration, not step chrome
a list of tasks with statuses, not a linear step bar

role.overview: GOLD task/step chrome: todo / doing / done. Not a loading spinner.
role.not_when: A task list they complete in any order (task_list), or an unknown wait (loading_indicator).

role.overview: A determinate bar when the amount of work is known.

size.overview: Highest in the size hierarchy — the easiest to hit.
size.apply_when: The view's main instance, or full-width on a small viewport.
size.not_when: A dense toolbar or a third option next to the main control.

size.apply_when: Ordinary use in forms, pages, and chrome.
size.not_when: The only control on a mobile screen that should span the width.

size.overview: Lowest in the size hierarchy — densest.
size.apply_when: Inline or chrome that sits beside content.
size.not_when: The page's primary instance, or a control under 44×44.

composition.overview: Each step has a name, not only a number.

state.not_when: A skipped required step with no name.

state.overview: This step is the current one.
state.not_when: A highlight with no accessible current.
A tick that is the only cue and not named.

accessibility.overview: The current step is named and exposed.
This is not an indeterminate wait graphic.

keyboard.overview: If steps are links to completed steps, they are in the tab order. Decorative pips are not fake stops.
keyboard.apply_when: A stepper they can go back through.
keyboard.not_when: Every pip is a tab stop with no name.
